name: Eden Diaz
life: “I still remember watching beach performers from under the rail.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Eden by a small Thursday habit. Eden pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I always thought she was diving. From my wheelchair she's clearly reaching for somebody.
appearance: Eden is easy to recognize by short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat and an aquiline nose and a square chin. Usually dressed in a moss-green cardigan with a small enamel bird on the lapel, Eden presses the lips together to keep a smile in when listening.
personality: Eden uses precise names for tools and very approximate names for feelings. People who know Eden well listen to what gets repaired after a difficult conversation.
agenda: To show the sculpted hand from wheelchair height.
family: Billie Morrow is Eden’s second cousin. Eden gets to change the plan. Billie offers the first invitation. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Saturday keys*, Billie says, “I returned the ring inside a soup tin to keep it dry.”
connections: Lara Ng. A lower view of the mural makes the possible second figure easier to see.

reactions.response: Eden asks the original model which part has been misunderstood.

reactions.response: Eden offers an ordinary errand that lets the distressed person leave without being followed by an audience.
